CHAPTER 04 / WEBFRONT

Calling C++ from TypeScript

The calling protocol, data representation and error handling.

Notation conventions

Function names, types, commands, options and filenames appear in monospace, for example describe, wf test or main.cpp. Italics introduce a term at its definition. Code blocks give the fragments to enter; the preceding text states their location and prerequisites.

Waiting for a call result ↓Representing the grid ↓Call ordering and errors ↓

Waiting for a call result

webFront.ready is a promise that resolves after the WebSocket handshake acknowledgement. The programme waits for this connection before calling life.step with the current grid.

A JavaScript call to C++ always returns a Promise, even when the C++ function returns void. Await the promise or handle its rejection. The following fragment belongs inside an async function; cells is the starter’s grid.

SOURCE
try {
    await webFront.ready;
    const step = webFront.cppFunction('life.step');
    const next = await step(cells);
    // Update your React state with next.
} catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
    // Stop playback and show the error in your UI.
}

Representing the grid

A std::bitset<1024> is transmitted as a 128-byte Uint8Array. Within each byte, the least-significant bit represents the first cell. The size must be exact and any padding bits must be zero.

The bridge supports scalars, strings, tuples, numeric typed arrays and packed bitsets. It does not transport arbitrary JavaScript objects. String lengths are encoded in 16 bits.

Call ordering and errors

Only one generation calculation should be outstanding. Wait for its reply before requesting another. If a reset occurs in the meantime, the old reply must no longer update the grid; the starter uses a revision number for this purpose.

A missing function, a C++ exception or disconnection rejects the promise. The programme must then stop playback and display the error.

In the opposite direction, ui.jsFunction(name) ignores the result, whereas ui.jsFunction<R>(name) returns a std::future<R>. Callbacks execute on the server thread, where blocking work delays other operations.

↗ Exercise

Examine nextGeneration in the starter. Identify the connection wait, reply validation and rejection of an outdated reply.
